sourceBook: Michael C. Gemignani, Elementary Topology, Second Edition
privateInputPolicy: Supplied PDF, full-page scans, crops and private comparisons remain local inputs; only provenance and graphic rectangles are recorded.
reuseVerification: Contract-and-slide, fixed-endpoint arc and pasted homotopy styles each optimize distinct parameterized mathematical Substances using the same Style instance.

Native homotopyCylinderView and homotopyFamilyStyle support ordinary domain fibers, optional abstract boundaries, endpoint hatching, image leaders and adjustable view dimensions; defaults of reviewed 11.1–4 remain unchanged.
Closed disks, intervals, products, continuous maps, ImageOf, CorestrictionOf, ExtensionOf and UnionOf are reused. Coarse homotopy and relative-homotopy predicates remain independent of shape data.
Mathematical parabolic arcs are converted exactly to native cubic Path coordinates by reusable ParabolicArcView; no raw SVG/image wrappers are used.

mathematics: Identity at time1 contracts continuously to the center at1/2, then slides continuously to the horizontal constant point (1/2,0) at time0.
The source unit disk and its positive-radius radial images are closed; constant images are singleton sets. Actual product fibers use Y×[0,1] and the correct mathematical slice parameters.
visualFidelity: Four source cylinder slices, endpoint hatching, slice markers, axis-aligned concentric images, three marked points and all eleven labels are preserved.
The source cylinder places the label3/4 below1/2; this exceptional source layout is isolated in Style and does not alter the actual mathematical parameters.

sourceCorrection.source: The graphic labels the domain Y × [0,0], places 3/4 below 1/2, and shows the horizontal constant point (1/2,0). Printed page 235 describes the vertical point (0,1/2) and a differently oriented piecewise family; page 236 reverses its endpoint claim.
sourceCorrection.mathematicalProgram: Uses the coherent family matching the picture: H(p,r) = (1 − 2r)(1/2,0) for r ≤ 1/2 and (2r − 1)p for r ≥ 1/2. Its domain is Y × [0,1], with the identity at 1 and the constant at 0.
sourceCorrection.visibleFigure: Preserves the supplied labels. The erroneous domain text and nonmonotone cylinder order are explicit overrides in Style.

mathematics: Two injective parabolic arcs have the same endpoints and enclose the removed point P. Linear interpolation through their normal displacements is a homotopy relative to the closed endpoint pair{0,1} in the plane.
After corestricting both arcs to the punctured plane, they are not homotopic relative to those endpoints. This is not an assertion of nonhomotopy when endpoints may move.
visualFidelity: Shared left/lower and right/upper endpoints, the interior P, the visible family of arcs, upper/lower image labels and the upper endpoint leader preserve source incidence and composition.

sourceCorrection.source: The prose says the two functions are not homotopic after removing P without explicitly retaining their common endpoints.
sourceCorrection.mathematicalProgram: Asserts the obstruction for homotopies relative to {0,1}. Unrestricted paths from the contractible interval into the connected punctured plane are homotopic.
sourceCorrection.visibleFigure: Preserves the source labels and fixed-endpoint illustration.

mathematics: H1 runs from g at0 to f at1; H2 runs from k at0 to g at1. Rescaled pasting on the two closed half intervals gives H from k at0 to f at1, agreeing at the common g slice.
Each domain fiber is an explicit product with its singleton parameter; ImageOf gives f(X),g(X),k(X) as subsets of Y.
